Every `fleetd` command, from `fleetd help` in the binary this site was built with.

| Exit code | Means |
|---|---|
| 0 | ok |
| 1 | failed: a check did not pass |
| 2 | usage error |
| 3 | refused |
| 4 | the hub or the node is unreachable |
| 78 | `listen` only: the hub refused the key |

## Commands {#commands}

### fleetd version {#version}

```text
fleetd version
```

print the fleetd version and protocol

### fleetd help {#help}

```text
fleetd help
```

show this message

### fleetd update {#update}

```text
fleetd update [--check] [--channel <c>]
```

replace this fleetd with the latest release


## Setting up {#setting-up}

On the hub machine.

### fleetd init {#init}

```text
fleetd init [--yes] [--home <dir>] [--listen <host:port>] [--url <url>]
    [--git-identity "Name <email>"] [--no-service] [--unit-suffix <s>]
```

set up fleetd step by step in a terminal: the hub on this machine (home default `~/.fleetd/hub`, kept running by a systemd or launchd user service), where it listens (your tailnet when there is one), the claude and gh logins, the machines that run agents, a first project and the desktop app, then `fleetd doctor`. Run it again to check and repair; it keeps what works. `--yes` takes every default. Without a terminal and without `--yes` it only sets up the hub. `--url` is how devices reach the hub (default http://\<listen\>); `--git-identity` is the commit author for every machine (the GitHub noreply address for public repos); `--no-service` prepares everything but leaves starting the hub to you

### fleetd init {#init-join}

```text
fleetd init --join <hub url> --code <code> [--machine-id <id>] [--git-identity "Name <email>"] [--rejoin]
    [--claude-config-dir <dir>]
```

make this machine a worker of that hub, without SSH from the hub: the command `fleetd pair --worker` prints on the hub. Run again, it keeps the node's enrolment and repairs the rest; `--rejoin` enrols again with a new code

### fleetd doctor {#doctor}

```text
fleetd doctor [--home <dir>]
```

run every setup check on the hub now and print each problem with its fix

### fleetd uninstall {#uninstall}

```text
fleetd uninstall [--home <dir>] [--purge]
```

stop and remove the hub's service; its data stays unless `--purge`, which also removes what an older fleetd installed for T3 Code

### fleetd machine add {#machine-add}

```text
fleetd machine add <ssh-host> | --local [--machine-id <id>] [--tags a,b] [--dry-run] [--no-service]
    [--hub-url <url>] [--ssh-config <file>] [--home <hub home>] [--unit-suffix <s>]
    [--claude-config-dir <dir>]
```

set up a machine that runs agents, over SSH (`--local`: this machine): copies this fleetd there, checks its claude (installed, version \>=2.1.300, \<2.2.0, logged in), enrolls the node and runs it as a user service, then waits until the machine is online; prints every command first, `--dry-run` only prints (for a fresh machine, without connecting); `--no-service` enrolls the node but writes no service and prints how to run it; safe to run again

### fleetd machine remove {#machine-remove}

```text
fleetd machine remove <id> [--purge] [--home <hub home>]
```

stop and remove the node's service on the machine and revoke its key on the hub; `--purge` also deletes `~/.fleetd/node` and `~/.fleetd/claude.env` there, and what an older fleetd installed for T3 Code

### fleetd pair {#pair}

```text
fleetd pair [--name <device>] [--home <dir>]
```

print a one-time code (15 min) that pairs the desktop app with this hub; the app on this machine pairs by itself

### fleetd pair {#pair-worker}

```text
fleetd pair --worker <machine-id> [--home <dir>]
```

print the one command that makes another machine a worker of this hub, with a one-time code (15 min): for a machine the hub can't reach over SSH


## Projects {#projects}

### fleetd project add {#project-add}

```text
fleetd project add [<path|github-url>] [--machine <id>] [--title <t>] [--dest <dir>]
    [--use-existing] [--yes] [--home <dir>] [--hub <url>]
```

add a project: a checkout on a machine (this one by default), or a GitHub repo cloned onto one (the least busy worker by default), with progress; then its CI, merge rules and what the lead will need. No argument: pick one

### fleetd project list {#project-list}

```text
fleetd project list [--machine <id>] [--home <dir>] [--hub <url>]
```

### fleetd project stop {#project-stop}

```text
fleetd project stop <machine>/<project> [--yes] [--home <dir>] [--hub <url>]
```

stop everything running in it: its agents are cancelled, the lead and its chat stay, and the chat says so

### fleetd project remove {#project-remove}

```text
fleetd project remove <machine>/<project> [--yes] [--home <dir>] [--hub <url>]
```

stop its agents and forget it; its files, branches and worktrees stay

### fleetd project set {#project-set}

```text
fleetd project set <machine>/<project> --max-agents <n> [--pause-extras] [--home <dir>] [--hub <url>]
```

### fleetd project set {#project-set-fleet-cap}

```text
fleetd project set --fleet-cap <n> [--home <dir>] [--hub <url>]
```

the most agents the project runs at once (its lead not counted), or the fleet's cap on running turns (admin key); more wait queued and start as slots free. Lowering stops nothing; `--pause-extras` has the newest agents above the new max push their work and wait


## Running by hand {#running-by-hand}

:::tip
Run `fleetd init --no-service` before `fleetd hub start`: it writes the setup the other commands read. The whole order is in [Run a second fleet on one machine](/docs/config-and-files#second-fleet).
:::

### fleetd hub start {#hub-start}

```text
fleetd hub start [--home <dir>] [--listen <host:port>] [--queue-ttl <seconds>] [--retro-model <model>]
```

run the hub (default home `~/.fleetd/hub`, listen 127.0.0.1:4790, writes to an offline machine wait 24 h, intents without a project are routed by the claude CLI with claude-haiku-5-5)

### fleetd hub key create {#hub-key-create}

```text
fleetd hub key create --name <name> --role <read|operate|admin> --machines <'*'|id,id> [--out <file>] [--home <dir>]
```

create an agent key for the MCP endpoint; prints the key once, or with `--out` writes it to a new file (0600) and prints the file's path

### fleetd hub key create {#hub-key-create-agent}

```text
fleetd hub key create --agent <name> [--machines <'*'|id,id>] [--out <file>] [--home <dir>]
```

a named agent's key, to write in a project's chat (`fleetd chat --key-file`): its messages show as that agent's, never yours. Operate on every machine unless `--machines`. Written to a new file (0600), \<hub home\>/keys/\<name\>.key unless `--out`; prints only the file's path

### fleetd hub key create {#hub-key-create-human}

```text
fleetd hub key create --human --name <device> [--role <role>] [--machines <'*'|id,id>] [--out <file>] [--home <dir>]
```

a key for a person's device (the desktop app): what it answers is recorded as the human's; role defaults to operate on every machine

### fleetd hub key list {#hub-key-list}

```text
fleetd hub key list [--home <dir>]
```

### fleetd hub key revoke {#hub-key-revoke}

```text
fleetd hub key revoke <keyId> [--home <dir>]
```

takes effect at once, also on a running hub

### fleetd hub token create {#hub-token-create}

```text
fleetd hub token create --machine <id> [--home <dir>]
```

print a one-time enrollment token (15 min) for `fleetd node join`

### fleetd hub github-webhook {#hub-github-webhook}

```text
fleetd hub github-webhook (--url <public url>/github | --off) [--hub <url> --key-file <path> | --home <dir>]
```

let GitHub tell the hub about pull requests, checks and pushes on the train's repos as they happen (admin key). It needs a URL GitHub can reach that forwards to this hub, which fleetd never creates; without one the hub syncs with GitHub on its own

### fleetd node join {#node-join}

```text
fleetd node join --hub <url> (--token <token> | --token-file <file|->) --machine <id> [--tags a,b]
    [--name <name>] [--home <dir>] [--enroll-only] [--claude-config-dir <dir>]
```

enroll this machine with the hub, then keep its link up (node home default `~/.fleetd/node`); `--token-file` - reads the token from stdin; `--enroll-only` exits once the hub has accepted this node; sessions use your own claude setup (`~/.claude`) unless `--claude-config-dir` names a dedicated one

### fleetd node run {#node-run}

```text
fleetd node run [--home <dir>]
```

keep the link up for a machine that has joined

### fleetd listen {#listen}

```text
fleetd listen --hub <url> --key-file <path> (--exec '<cmd>' | --post <url>)
    [--types a,b] [--machines a,b] [--name <name>]
```

deliver hub events, at least once and in order, to a command (one event's JSON on stdin) or a URL; the cursor lives in `~/.fleetd/listen/<name>.cursor` (name default "default"). Exits 78 when the hub refuses the key.

### fleetd retro run {#retro-run}

```text
fleetd retro run --hub <url> --key-file <path> [--window 14d] [--advise]
```

run the retro now: one claude -p turn over the window's incidents (1-28 days) proposes playbook changes; `--advise` only suggests them

### fleetd prompts list {#prompts-list}

```text
fleetd prompts list [--project <machine>/<project>] [--home <dir>]
```

every prompt fleetd sends a model, which text is in effect, and "update" where a release changed the default you edited

### fleetd prompts show {#prompts-show}

```text
fleetd prompts show <id> [--project <machine>/<project>] [--default] [--home <dir>]
```

### fleetd prompts show {#prompts-show-session}

```text
fleetd prompts show --session <machine>/<thread> [--home <dir>]
```

the text in effect (or the shipped one), or exactly what a session was told

### fleetd prompts edit {#prompts-edit}

```text
fleetd prompts edit <id> [--project <machine>/<project>] [--home <dir>]
```

edit it in $VISUAL or $EDITOR; warns when a placeholder or a safety rule is gone

### fleetd prompts reset {#prompts-reset}

```text
fleetd prompts reset <id> [--project <machine>/<project>] [--home <dir>]
```

### fleetd prompts diff {#prompts-diff}

```text
fleetd prompts diff <id> [--project <machine>/<project>] [--home <dir>]
```

shipped vs yours; after a release changed it, what changed in each

### fleetd instructions {#instructions}

```text
fleetd instructions show|edit [--project <machine>/<project>] [--home <dir>]
```

your custom instructions, appended to every lead and task

### fleetd time {#time}

```text
fleetd time [<order>|<project>] [--since 7d] [--spans <rule>] [--json] [--hub <url> --key-file <path> | --home <dir>]
```

where agents' time went: an order's critical path, agent time by category, the slowest commands and the findings; a project by id or title (\<machine\>/\<project\> when two machines have one), the whole fleet with neither. `--since` takes 1h to 400d, a date or an ISO time; `--spans` \<rule\> lists the spans a finding points at. On the hub machine it needs no `--hub` or `--key-file`

### fleetd time {#time-retention}

```text
fleetd time --retention <days> [--hub <url> --key-file <path> | --home <dir>]
```

keep 1-365 days of timelines (admin key); daily totals are kept 400 days

### fleetd status {#status}

```text
fleetd status [<order>|<project>] [--watch] [--json] [--hub <url> --key-file <path> | --home <dir>]
```

progress (verified plus work in flight), why it fell, the critical path it waits on, what is slower than usual, what changed since you last looked, health and risks; for an order (W41), a project by id or title (\<machine\>/\<project\> when two machines have one), or the whole fleet. `--watch` prints each new version as the hub sends it; stale parts say so. On the hub machine it needs no `--hub` or `--key-file`

### fleetd steer {#steer}

```text
fleetd steer <W|T> "<text>" [--now] [--wait] --key-file <human key> [--hub <url> | --home <dir>]
```

steer an order's lead (W41) or one agent (T88) mid-run. Plain: it lands at the agent's next step, after the tool it is running returns. `--now` stops that step and delivers at once. `--wait` follows the receipt: exit 0 acknowledged, 1 not acknowledged, withdrawn or failed. Without `--hub` it uses the hub on this machine

### fleetd steer withdraw {#steer-withdraw}

```text
fleetd steer withdraw S<n> --key-file <human key> [--hub <url> | --home <dir>]
```

take back a steer the agent has not taken in yet

### fleetd steers {#steers}

```text
fleetd steers [W|T] --key-file <human key> [--hub <url> | --home <dir>]
```

recent steers and their receipts

### fleetd chat {#chat}

```text
fleetd chat <machine>/<project> "<text>" [--wait | --follow] [--key-file <key>] [--hub <url> | --home <dir>]
```

write to a project's lead, as the app does: it starts the lead's next turn, or lands at its next step while it works. `--wait` prints the lead's reply when its turn ends; `--follow` streams it as it is written. Exit 0 it replied, 1 its turn ended without a reply. A human key writes as you; an agent key as that agent, by its name. Without `--key-file`, as you, the owner of the hub on this machine

### fleetd chat history {#chat-history}

```text
fleetd chat history <project> [--page <n>] [--key-file <key>] [--hub <url> | --home <dir>]
```

the project's chat: who wrote each message, when, and what; the newest page, older ones with `--page`


## Lead-side commands {#lead-side-commands}

A lead uses its fleetd tools; these are for you, inside a project workspace.

### fleetd brief create {#brief-create}

```text
fleetd brief create --workstream <W> (--json '<Brief>' | --file <path>) [--amend <decision key>]
```

freeze the brief of a draft workstream and start it; `--amend` changes a frozen brief once the human said yes in chat and you logged it with decide

### fleetd request secret {#request-secret}

```text
fleetd request secret --key <k> --sink env:<machine>:<path>|file:<machine>:<path> [--env-name <N>]
    --text <t> [--workstream <W>]
```

the human enters it in a masked field in the project's chat, sealed to that machine; an env: sink writes the line \<N\>=\<value\> (N defaults to the key uppercased, . and - as \_). You get its fingerprint in a wake, never the value

### fleetd gated run {#gated-run}

```text
fleetd gated run --class irreversible|money|credential --argv '<json array>' --reason <r> [--cwd <abs>]
    [--secret-env NAME=<secret key> ...] [--timeout <sec>] [--workstream <W>]
```

a command the node runs exactly as stored, in the project workspace by default, only after a human approves it in the project's chat; secrets come from the node's own sinks. The result arrives in a wake

### fleetd request withdraw {#request-withdraw}

```text
fleetd request withdraw <Q>
```

take back a secret request or a command approval the human said in chat is not needed

### fleetd decide {#decide}

```text
fleetd decide --key <k> --value <v> [--why <w>] [--scope project|workstream] [--workstream <W>]
```

log a decision you made yourself

### fleetd status set {#status-set}

```text
fleetd status set "<one line>" [--workstream <W>]
```

### fleetd decisions search {#decisions-search}

```text
fleetd decisions search "<query>"
```

### fleetd task spawn {#task-spawn}

```text
fleetd task spawn --workstream <W> --title <t> --prompt <p> [--kind write|read|review] [--areas a,b]
    [--model <m>] [--effort low|medium|high|max] [--tier S|M|L]
    [--serves done:<n>|issue:<ref>|defect:<text>|decision:<key>] [--pr <url>] [--qa] [--item P<n>]
```

delegate work to a subagent; writers need `--areas` and `--serves` and get their own branch; a review task needs `--pr`, and `--qa` marks it a QA run; `--item` links it to that plan item

### fleetd task list {#task-list}

```text
fleetd task list [--state <s>] [--workstream <W>]
```

### fleetd task status {#task-status}

```text
fleetd task status <T>
```

### fleetd task message {#task-message}

```text
fleetd task message <T> "<text>" [--now]
```

steer a running task (at its next step; `--now` stops its current step), answer a waiting one, or continue an ended one

### fleetd task cancel {#task-cancel}

```text
fleetd task cancel <T> [--reason <r>]
```

### fleetd claim done {#claim-done}

```text
fleetd claim done --workstream <W> [--close-over "<why>"]
```

fleetd runs the workstream's done-when checks itself; only all of them passing makes it done (exit 1 when a check did not pass)

### fleetd review verdict {#review-verdict}

```text
fleetd review verdict --task <T> --sha <full head SHA> --blocking <n> --non-blocking <n> --summary "<s>"
    [--baseline <n> --candidate <n>]
```

the last step of a review task; a research judge also reports its metric for the baseline and the candidate, and fleetd computes GO, STOP or INCONCLUSIVE

### fleetd change enqueue {#change-enqueue}

```text
fleetd change enqueue --pr <url> [--task <T>] [--workstream <W>] [--serves <s>] [--tier S|M|L]
    [--item P<n>]
```

put a PR on its repo's merge train (a write task's PR goes on by itself); its body needs a 'Source: \<serves\>' line. Only the train merges. `--item` links the PR to that plan item

### fleetd change status {#change-status}

```text
fleetd change status <X>
```

### fleetd plan milestone {#plan-milestone}

```text
fleetd plan milestone "<title>" [--position <n>]
```

### fleetd plan add {#plan-add}

```text
fleetd plan add "<title>" --milestone M<n> [--workstream <W>] [--must|--polish] [--size s|m|l]
    [--after P1,P2] [--pr <url>] [--check <n>] [--why "<note>"] [--steer S<n>]
```

### fleetd plan edit {#plan-edit}

```text
fleetd plan edit P<n> [--title <t>] [--size s|m|l] [--must|--polish] [--milestone M<n>]
    [--workstream <W>] [--after P1,P2] [--pr +<url>|--pr=-<url>] [--check +<n>|--check=-<n>]
    [--position <n>] [--why "<note>"] [--steer S<n>]
```

### fleetd plan drop {#plan-drop}

```text
fleetd plan drop P<n> (--why "<reason>" | --steer S<n>)
```

### fleetd plan show {#plan-show}

```text
fleetd plan show [--workstream <W>]
```

keep the project's plan: milestones of must or polish items sized s, m or l (relative size, never hours). Link work with `--item`; only fleetd marks an item done, once its PRs merged through the train and its done-when checks passed. Changing scope after a milestone's first 10 minutes needs `--why`, and the status view shows it as a marker. `--steer` S\<n\> says the human's steer asked for it: it stands in for `--why` and acknowledges the steer

### fleetd inventory {#inventory}

```text
fleetd inventory
```

the project's open work ranked: failing checks, open issues (gh), open requests and TODO/FIXME markers; with nothing left that has a value source and no open child, the project's finish-all workstream goes idle

### fleetd workstream open {#workstream-open}

```text
fleetd workstream open --text "<intent>" [--template bugfix|feature|research|finish-all] [--serves <s>]
```

open a workstream for work taken from the chat: a draft to brief

### fleetd workstream spawn {#workstream-spawn}

```text
fleetd workstream spawn --text "<intent>" --serves issue:<#n|url>|defect:<text>|done:<n>
    [--template bugfix|feature|research]
```

a finish-all lead starts a child workstream for one item with a value source

:::note
lead-side commands reach the hub through the local node (FLEETD\_NODE\_SOCK, default `~/.fleetd/node/node.sock`); exit 0 ok, 1 checks failed, 2 usage, 3 refused, 4 hub unreachable
:::
